A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PSBD and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and additional evaluations.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction-shift studies and backdoor-detection experiments on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet, including low-poisoning results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds GTSRB results, feature-map analyses, adaptive-attack evaluations and AUROC comparisons.

M1.justification: The PSBD detector retains its PSU calculation, adaptive dropout selection and validation-based threshold. Appendix F adds an auxiliary attack-training procedure: BadNets and WaNet are adapted using a weighted combination of the backdoor loss and a PSU penalty. This changes attack construction without redesigning PSBD.

E1.justification: v2 adds GTSRB traffic-sign classification to CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet. Appendix F also introduces attacks optimized with full knowledge of PSBD, extending the evaluated adversarial scenarios beyond those in v1. VGG and low-poisoning evaluations were already present.

E2.justification: CD-L joins the existing detector comparisons in Tables 1 and A4, including the retained datasets, and participates in the new AUROC comparison. The original five baselines remain; SS is the renamed Spectral Signature baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix G adds AUROC evaluation beyond the retained TPR/FPR operating points. Appendix F introduces a controlled adaptive-attack protocol using PSU-penalized training, weights of 0.2, 0.5 and 0.9, and penalty computation every 50 iterations. The documented training schedules for the original datasets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds clean/backdoor feature-map comparisons with and without dropout, expanded in Appendix C, and adaptive-attack robustness tests in Appendix F. These examine the proposed mechanism and resistance to deliberate evasion. Conversely, v1's Figure 4 comparing Tiny ImageNet training with and without augmentation is removed, although its discussion remains.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported trial count from three to ten. v2 removes the standard deviations previously reported throughout Tables 1 and A4, stating that variances are small, although a sentence describing bracketed standard deviations remains. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New GTSRB, CD-L, adaptive-attack and AUROC entries substantially expand the results. Existing values also change: Table A4 reports PSBD's CIFAR-10 Blend TPR/FPR as 0.899/0.176 instead of 0.811/0.163, alongside the revised trial count. Table 1 changes SCP's Adaptive-Blend results while retaining the existing PSBD means. These are revised reported results, not evidence of an improved detector under identical protocols.

T1.justification: Appendix F newly formalizes the adaptive attack through the PSU-based loss and its weighted combination with the backdoor-training loss. The existing prediction-shift and PSU definitions remain equivalent. No theorem, proof or theoretical justification of neuron bias is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: prediction shift distinguishes clean and poisoned data, neuron bias explains the phenomenon, and PSBD provides effective uncertainty-based detection. The additional experiments support these existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets feature-map similarity as confirmation of neuron bias and explains adaptive-attack resistance through selecting a different dropout rate. It adds an explanation for weaker ISSBA performance. Appendix H revises the limitations to acknowledge limited theoretical foundations and untested generalization to ViT and larger datasets.

D1.justification: v2 supplies GTSRB dataset/training specifications, CD-L implementation provenance and adaptive-attack settings. It omits v1's specific 95th-epoch checkpoint choice, explicit flip/crop augmentation choices and Label-Consistent trigger-transparency detail. These omissions do not establish changed execution settings. The PSBD code link and computational-environment description remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The defense discussion adds descriptions of Spectral Signatures, STRIP and SCP. Newly cited works include randomized channel shuffling, optimized scaled prediction consistency, CatchBackdoor, ViT and GTSRB; Fine-pruning is no longer cited. The central positioning around model-level rather than input-level uncertainty remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose are retained. Local revisions condense the pilot-study explanation, expand the introduction and defense discussion, rewrite limitations, reorganize appendix subsections and update affiliations and acknowledgements. The Broader Impact section is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, new feature-map figures and tables are introduced, and comparison tables gain dataset blocks and a CD-L column. The benign MC-Dropout panel moves from Figure 2 to Appendix Figure A1; the augmentation-comparison figure is removed.

improvement.justification: The adaptive-attack tests, AUROC comparison and additional dataset/baseline coverage make v2's empirical claims more assessable. The gain is tempered by removed standard deviations and implementation details. Reporting consistency also worsens: Tables 1 and A4 give different SCP Adaptive-Blend values despite A4's statement that those results are reused. Overall, the expanded validation provides a limited net improvement.
